title: Windows PrivEsc Explorer
description: Structured Windows privilege escalation assessment techniques for authorised security testing.

techniques.name: Writable Service Executable
techniques.summary: A privileged Windows service executes a binary that can be modified by a lower-privileged user.
found: Service executes as LocalSystem or another privileged identity
Current user or one of their groups has Modify, Write, or FullControl over the service executable
requires: A service running with elevated privileges
A lower-privileged user can modify or replace the service executable
The service will execute again through a legitimate start, restart, boot, or recovery condition
validation: Confirm effective write or replacement permissions
Determine whether the service executes again under a realistic authorised condition
Prefer ACL and service configuration evidence over replacing the executable
detection: Monitor unexpected service starts and restarts
Use file integrity monitoring for privileged service directories
remediation: Remove unnecessary write permissions from the service executable
Protect the parent directory from lower-privileged modification
Apply least privilege to the service account
Monitor privileged service binaries for unexpected modification

techniques.name: Writable Service Directory
techniques.summary: A lower-privileged user can modify a directory containing resources trusted by a privileged Windows service.
found: Privileged service executable or dependencies are stored in a writable directory
Users, Authenticated Users, Everyone, or another lower-privileged group has dangerous directory rights
requires: A privileged service consumes resources from the directory
The lower-privileged identity has effective create, delete, rename, replace, modify, or equivalent control
The controlled resource affects privileged service execution
validation: Confirm which resources are loaded from the directory
Evaluate directory rights separately from file rights
Determine whether parent-directory permissions permit replacement
Avoid changing production files during initial validation
detection: Alert on unexpected file creation or replacement
Monitor service binary and dependency changes
remediation: Restrict write access to privileged service directories
Remove broad Modify and FullControl permissions
Separate user-writable data from executable content

techniques.name: Weak Service Object Permissions
techniques.summary: A lower-privileged identity has security-sensitive control over a privileged Windows service object.
found: Service security descriptor grants excessive rights to a lower-privileged principal
Current user may be able to change service configuration or other security-sensitive service properties
requires: A privileged service
Dangerous service-object rights assigned to a lower-privileged identity
The granted rights provide meaningful control over privileged service behaviour
validation: Determine which rights apply to the current user and groups
Identify whether those rights permit security-sensitive service control
Do not change production service configuration merely to prove the issue
remediation: Grant service-management rights only to approved administrative identities
Review inherited or delegated service-management permissions

techniques.name: Unquoted Service Path
techniques.summary: A privileged service uses an unquoted executable path containing spaces and a lower-privileged user controls a candidate path Windows may evaluate during executable resolution.
found: Service executable path contains spaces
Executable path is not correctly quoted
A candidate directory or path component is writable by the current user
requires: Unquoted service executable path containing spaces
Privileged service execution context
A writable candidate location relevant to Windows path parsing
An execution opportunity
validation: Confirm the executable path is actually unquoted
Determine the candidate executable paths Windows could evaluate
Check permissions on each candidate location
Do not create candidate executables during routine validation
detection: Audit privileged services for unquoted paths
Monitor executable creation in unusual parent directories
Monitor service starts involving unexpected executables
remediation: Restrict write permissions on parent directories

techniques.name: Writable Service Configuration Resource
techniques.summary: A privileged service consumes configuration or helper resources that can be modified by a lower-privileged identity.
found: Service uses a writable configuration file, helper script, plugin, or supporting resource
The resource influences privileged service behaviour
requires: Privileged service
Lower-privileged write access to a trusted resource
The resource meaningfully influences service execution
validation: Identify how the service consumes the resource
Establish whether the resource influences privileged behaviour
Prefer configuration evidence over modifying the resource
detection: Monitor unexpected modifications in application directories
remediation: Separate writable data from privileged configuration
Run the service with minimum required privilege

techniques.name: Writable Scheduled Task Action
techniques.summary: A scheduled task running under an elevated identity executes a file that can be modified by a lower-privileged user.
found: Scheduled task runs as SYSTEM, administrator, or another privileged identity
Task action references a lower-privileged writable executable or script
requires: Privileged scheduled task
Writable task action or trusted dependency
Task will execute through its configured trigger or another authorised activation condition
validation: Avoid modifying the scheduled task action
detection: Alert on unexpected changes to scripts executed as SYSTEM

techniques.name: SeImpersonatePrivilege
techniques.summary: The current token contains SeImpersonatePrivilege, which may become security-sensitive when the process can obtain a suitable privileged impersonation context.
found: whoami /priv shows SeImpersonatePrivilege
requires: SeImpersonatePrivilege is available in the relevant token
A suitable privileged authentication or token context exists
The surrounding operating-system and application conditions permit meaningful impersonation
validation: Record whether the privilege is enabled or disabled
Identify why the account has the privilege
Determine whether a suitable privileged token or authentication context exists
Do not report the privilege alone as confirmed SYSTEM escalation
detection: Monitor suspicious token-manipulation activity where telemetry is available
remediation: Reduce exposure of privileged authentication contexts

techniques.name: SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege
techniques.summary: The current security context has the ability to assign primary tokens under applicable Windows security rules.
found: whoami /priv shows SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege
requires: Relevant privilege is available
Suitable token and process conditions exist
Windows security controls permit the intended token operation
validation: Determine why the identity requires the privilege
Identify whether suitable token conditions actually exist

techniques.name: SeBackupPrivilege
techniques.summary: The current identity has backup rights that can bypass selected normal file-read restrictions during authorised backup operations.
found: whoami /priv shows SeBackupPrivilege
requires: SeBackupPrivilege is available
Security-sensitive resources are accessible through applicable backup semantics
Access creates a meaningful privilege or confidentiality impact
validation: Identify why the account has backup rights
Determine which protected resources become accessible
Avoid extracting credential databases when metadata and access evidence are sufficient
detection: Monitor unusual access to sensitive operating-system files
remediation: Restrict backup rights to dedicated administrative identities

techniques.name: SeRestorePrivilege
techniques.summary: The current identity has restore rights capable of bypassing selected normal write restrictions during authorised restoration operations.
found: whoami /priv shows SeRestorePrivilege
requires: SeRestorePrivilege is available
The identity can affect a security-sensitive resource
The resource is trusted by a more privileged component
validation: Do not overwrite protected production resources to prove the condition
detection: Monitor modifications to protected operating-system and application resources

techniques.name: SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege
techniques.summary: The current identity can take ownership of securable objects under applicable Windows security rules.
found: whoami /priv shows SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege
requires: SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege is available
A security-sensitive object can be targeted
Ownership would provide meaningful control over a privileged resource
validation: Avoid changing production ownership merely to demonstrate impact
detection: Monitor ownership changes to privileged resources
remediation: Monitor security descriptor and ownership changes

mitre.name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification

techniques.name: SeDebugPrivilege
techniques.summary: The current identity has a highly sensitive process-debugging privilege that may allow extensive access to other processes.
found: whoami /priv shows SeDebugPrivilege
requires: SeDebugPrivilege is available in the relevant token
A higher-privileged target process is accessible under applicable protections
The access produces meaningful security impact
validation: Identify whether protected process restrictions apply
Avoid dumping sensitive process memory unless explicitly authorised
detection: Monitor sensitive process handle activity where endpoint telemetry supports it
remediation: Restrict SeDebugPrivilege to identities that require it
Use privileged access management for administrative debugging

techniques.name: SeLoadDriverPrivilege
techniques.summary: The current identity has the security-sensitive ability to load kernel drivers under applicable Windows policy and signing requirements.
found: whoami /priv shows SeLoadDriverPrivilege
requires: SeLoadDriverPrivilege is available
Driver-loading policy permits a relevant driver
The driver or driver configuration exposes meaningful privileged functionality
validation: Review driver signing and application-control policy
Do not load arbitrary or vulnerable drivers to prove impact
detection: Alert on unexpected kernel driver activity

techniques.name: Writable Privileged File
techniques.summary: A lower-privileged user can modify a file consumed or executed by a more privileged component.
found: Current user has dangerous rights over an executable, script, configuration file, plugin, or other privileged resource
requires: Lower-privileged write control
Higher-privileged consumer
The controlled file influences privileged behaviour
validation: Determine how the resource is used
Avoid changing the resource during initial validation
detection: Alert on unexpected changes by standard-user identities
remediation: Separate writable data from executable and configuration content

mitre.name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification

techniques.name: Writable Privileged Directory
techniques.summary: A lower-privileged user controls a directory from which a privileged application consumes security-sensitive resources.
found: Writable directory under Program Files, ProgramData, Windows, or a custom privileged application path
requires: A privileged consumer uses the directory
The current identity has effective write, create, replace, delete, or equivalent rights
The writable resource can influence privileged behaviour
validation: Do not report the writable directory by itself
Determine which controlled resources are trusted
Prefer ACL evidence over creating files
remediation: Separate user-generated data from privileged application content

mitre.name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification

techniques.name: Writable Security-Sensitive Registry Key
techniques.summary: A lower-privileged identity can modify registry configuration trusted by a privileged Windows component.
found: Current user has dangerous registry rights
The registry key controls privileged service, startup, application, or security-sensitive behaviour
requires: Lower-privileged registry write access
Privileged consumer
Registry values influence privileged behaviour
validation: Identify which values affect privileged behaviour
Do not modify registry values during routine validation

techniques.name: AlwaysInstallElevated
techniques.summary: Windows Installer policy is configured so that applicable MSI packages can install with elevated privileges when both required policy values are enabled.
found: HKCU AlwaysInstallElevated equals 1
HKLM AlwaysInstallElevated equals 1
requires: AlwaysInstallElevated enabled in the relevant HKCU policy location
AlwaysInstallElevated enabled in the relevant HKLM policy location
Windows Installer behaviour and policy are applicable
validation: Do not install a test MSI on a production system merely to confirm configuration impact
remediation: Ensure the policy is not enabled for both user and computer contexts

techniques.name: Writable PATH Directory
techniques.summary: A privileged process may resolve an executable from a PATH directory writable by a lower-privileged user.
found: A PATH directory is writable by the current user
A privileged application executes a command without a secure explicit path
requires: Writable PATH directory
Privileged process
Relevant executable lookup uses PATH
The writable location is selected before the intended executable or otherwise influences resolution
validation: Do not create replacement executables during initial validation
detection: Monitor executable creation in PATH directories
remediation: Remove user-writable directories from privileged PATH contexts

techniques.name: DLL Search Order Candidate
techniques.summary: A privileged application may search a lower-privileged writable location for a DLL loaded without a secure explicit path.
found: Privileged application requests a DLL by name or otherwise uses search-order resolution
A searched location is writable by the current user
requires: Privileged process
Relevant DLL lookup behaviour
Writable location in the effective DLL search path
No earlier trusted resolution prevents the candidate from being used
validation: Avoid dropping DLLs into production directories during initial validation
detection: Monitor DLL loads from user-writable locations
Monitor unexpected DLL creation in application directories

techniques.name: AutoLogon Credential Exposure
techniques.summary: Windows AutoLogon configuration may expose credentials for an identity with greater privileges than the current user.
found: AutoAdminLogon is configured
AutoLogon-related account information is present
requires: AutoLogon configuration exists
Credential material is accessible to the current identity
The exposed identity provides additional privilege or access
validation: Record account metadata without unnecessarily exposing passwords
Determine the privilege of the configured identity
detection: Monitor access to sensitive Winlogon registry values
remediation: Avoid plaintext or recoverable AutoLogon credentials

techniques.name: PowerShell History Credential Exposure
techniques.summary: PowerShell command history may contain secrets or credentials that provide access to a more privileged identity or system.
found: PSReadLine history contains password, token, secret, key, or credential-related command material
requires: Sensitive material exists in accessible history
The material remains valid or otherwise security-sensitive
The exposed identity or secret provides additional access
validation: Avoid printing complete secret values unnecessarily
Determine whether exposed material is still valid only where authorised
Redact secrets from screenshots and reports
detection: Prevent secret entry into interactive shells
remediation: Avoid passing secrets directly on command lines

techniques.name: Environment Variable Credential Exposure
techniques.summary: Environment variables accessible to the current user may contain credentials, API keys, tokens, or other sensitive material.
found: Environment-variable names or values indicate stored secrets
requires: Sensitive material is present
The current identity can access it
The secret provides additional privilege or access
validation: Determine the associated identity or service
detection: Review process and service environment configuration
remediation: Remove secrets from insecure environment configuration

techniques.name: Stored Credential Target
techniques.summary: Windows Credential Manager contains stored credential targets that may represent additional authenticated access.
found: cmdkey.exe /list returns stored targets
requires: Stored credential exists
The current security context can use it in an applicable authentication flow
The target identity or destination provides additional privilege or access
validation: Do not assume stored credentials can be extracted
Do not attempt authentication outside the authorised scope
remediation: Use managed identities or approved credential-management mechanisms
Apply least privilege to stored identities

techniques.name: UAC Elevated Administrator Context
techniques.summary: The current user is a local administrator operating with a filtered token, making UAC configuration relevant to elevation analysis.
found: Current identity belongs to Administrators
Current process is not operating at high integrity
requires: User already possesses administrative membership or equivalent administrative rights
UAC token filtering is applicable
An elevation path exists within the assessed configuration
validation: Do not treat UAC as a generic standard-user-to-administrator path
detection: Review UAC configuration against organisational baseline
remediation: Use standard-user accounts for routine activity
Use privileged access workstations or equivalent controls for administration

techniques.name: AppLocker Policy Gap
techniques.summary: Effective AppLocker policy may leave a relevant rule collection unconfigured or allow functionality inconsistent with the intended application-control boundary.
found: Relevant AppLocker collection is NotConfigured, AuditOnly, or contains unexpectedly broad allow rules
A tested executable or script is allowed where policy intent suggests it should be restricted
requires: AppLocker is part of the intended security boundary
The identified policy condition materially weakens that boundary
The allowed functionality is security-relevant in context
validation: Do not call an allowed executable a bypass without demonstrating policy impact
remediation: Avoid overly broad writable-path allow rules
Use publisher or appropriately controlled rules where practical

techniques.name: PowerShell FullLanguage in Restricted Endpoint
techniques.summary: PowerShell operates in FullLanguage mode on an endpoint whose intended security architecture expects Constrained Language Mode or equivalent application-control restrictions.
found: $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode returns FullLanguage
requires: The endpoint security baseline intends PowerShell language restrictions
FullLanguage materially expands functionality available to the lower-privileged user
Other controls do not provide the intended equivalent restriction
validation: Do not report FullLanguage alone as a vulnerability
remediation: Where required by the security model, enforce appropriate application control
Apply PowerShell restrictions as part of a broader endpoint-control strategy

techniques.name: Vulnerable Driver Candidate
techniques.summary: An installed third-party kernel driver may contain a known local security weakness or expose an unsafe privileged interface.
found: Third-party kernel driver is installed
Exact driver version or interface warrants security review
requires: Exact affected driver version or vulnerable implementation
Driver is loaded or otherwise reachable
Current user can interact with the relevant device or interface
Vendor advisory or controlled validation confirms applicability
validation: Confirm the driver is loaded or reachable
Do not load a vulnerable driver merely to demonstrate impact

techniques.name: Custom Privileged Application
techniques.summary: A custom or third-party application operates with elevated privileges and exposes lower-privileged writable resources or interfaces.
found: Custom application or service runs privileged
Lower-privileged users can influence files, configuration, plugins, IPC, named pipes, registry settings, or update mechanisms
requires: Privileged application
Lower-privileged influence over a trusted input or resource
The controlled input affects privileged behaviour
validation: Use configuration evidence before active manipulation
detection: Monitor changes to application configuration and plugins
Monitor unusual IPC interactions where supported

techniques.name: Privileged Named Pipe Exposure
techniques.summary: A privileged process exposes a named pipe whose access control or protocol may allow unsafe interaction from a lower-privileged identity.
found: Privileged process owns or serves a named pipe
Lower-privileged users can access the pipe
The protocol exposes security-sensitive functionality
requires: Privileged pipe server
Lower-privileged pipe access
Security-sensitive operation, authentication weakness, or unsafe impersonation behaviour
validation: Understand the protocol before sending test data
Do not report a pipe simply because it exists
detection: Monitor privileged application IPC where endpoint telemetry supports it
Review unusual client connections to administrative IPC
remediation: Validate client identity before privileged operations
Use least privilege for the pipe server

techniques.name: Privileged Autorun Resource
techniques.summary: A startup mechanism used by a privileged identity references a resource that can be modified by a lower-privileged user.
found: Machine-level autorun or privileged startup mechanism references a writable resource
requires: Higher-privileged startup consumer
Lower-privileged control over the referenced resource
The startup mechanism executes in the higher-privileged context
validation: Resolve the exact executable or script

techniques.name: Privileged Third-Party Software Candidate
techniques.summary: Installed third-party software with privileged components may expose a known or configuration-dependent local privilege escalation condition.
found: Third-party software is installed
Software includes privileged services, drivers, update agents, or management components
requires: Exact vulnerable version or insecure configuration
Relevant privileged component is installed
The current user can reach the affected attack surface
validation: Do not report based only on generic version matching
